question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Major European Wars and their primary theatre of conflict]
options: War of Spanish Succession (1701–1714) — fought largely in Western Europe including the Low Countries and Iberian Peninsula
War of Austrian Succession (1740–1748) — fought across Central Europe, Italy, and extended to colonial theatres in India and North America
Seven Years' War (1756–1763) — confined exclusively to the European continent with no overseas dimension
War of Spanish Succession — ended with the Treaty of Utrecht (1713)
wrong_fact: The Seven Years' War (1756–1763) is widely regarded as the first true 'world war'; it extended far beyond Europe to North America (French and Indian War), India (Carnatic Wars), the Caribbean, and Africa — it was not confined to Europe.
explanation: The Seven Years' War was fought on multiple continents. In India it directly influenced the Third Carnatic War (1756–1763) and led to the decisive decline of French power in India. The other options are correctly matched: the War of Spanish Succession was a pan-European conflict ending at Utrecht (1713), and the War of Austrian Succession (1740–1748) had colonial extensions including the First Carnatic War in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European War — corresponding Carnatic War in India]
options: War of Austrian Succession (1740–1748) — First Carnatic War (1746–1748)
Seven Years' War (1756–1763) — Third Carnatic War (1756–1763)
War of Spanish Succession (1701–1714) — Second Carnatic War (1749–1754)
Peace of Paris (1763) — ended both the Seven Years' War and the Third Carnatic War
wrong_fact: The War of Spanish Succession (1701–1714) did NOT trigger the Second Carnatic War. The Second Carnatic War (1749–1754) arose from local succession disputes in the Carnatic and Hyderabad and was not a direct extension of any European war; it was a period of Anglo-French proxy conflict in south India independent of a contemporary European war.
explanation: The First Carnatic War (1746–1748) was an extension of the War of Austrian Succession, and the Third Carnatic War (1756–1763) paralleled the Seven Years' War. The Second Carnatic War (1749–1754), however, was driven by Indian political rivalries (Muzaffar Jung vs Nasir Jung in Hyderabad; Chanda Sahib vs Muhammad Ali in Carnatic) and cannot be mapped to the War of Spanish Succession, which ended in 1714 — decades earlier.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Treaty ending a European War — its key territorial provision relevant to Anglo-French rivalry]
options: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) — restored status quo ante bellum; Madras returned to the British by France
Treaty of Paris (1763) — France ceded most of its Indian territories and trading posts to Britain, ending French imperial ambitions in India
Treaty of Utrecht (1713) — France ceded Newfoundland, Acadia (Nova Scotia), and Hudson Bay territories to Britain
Treaty of Fontainebleau (1762) — France ceded Louisiana to Spain to prevent it falling to Britain, signed before the Peace of Paris
wrong_fact: Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) the status quo ante was restored — but it was Madras that was returned to Britain BY France (France had captured Madras in 1746 under Dupleix). The option incorrectly implies Madras was returned to France; in reality, France returned Madras to Britain in exchange for Louisbourg in North America. The direction of the exchange is mis-stated.
explanation: Madras (Fort St. George) was captured by the French under La Bourdonnais and Dupleix in 1746. By the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), France agreed to restore Madras to Britain. The Treaty of Paris (1763) was indeed decisive for French India, and the Treaty of Utrecht (1713) did transfer significant North American territories to Britain. The Treaty of Fontainebleau (1762) was a secret Franco-Spanish treaty ceding Louisiana to Spain.
